description: Ask ChatGPT to make a page, a report or a small web app, and ShipStatic puts it online. You get a link you can share right away. You don't need an account. A site published without one stays up for 3 days, and its claim link lets you keep it. Want it private? Ask for built-in password protection, and visitors have to type the password before they see anything. If you have a ShipStatic account, connect it to keep every site, see them all and use your own domain.

positive.description: Publishing with no account. Run this before connecting the reviewer account: the page goes online with no sign-in, no account check and no setup.
positive.prompt: Make a one-page site for my bakery and give me a link I can share.
positive.expected_behavior: A deploy card with a live *.shipstatic.com link and a claim link. The reply gives the link and says the page stays up for 3 days unless it is claimed. ChatGPT does not ask to connect an account. Opening the link shows the bakery page.

positive.description: Built-in password protection, still with no account. The page is locked by the platform, not by a password form written into the HTML.
positive.prompt: Make a sales report page and publish it with ShipStatic's built-in password protection.
positive.expected_behavior: A deploy card with a live link, a claim link and a password chip. The reply tells the password. Opening the link shows an unlock page; entering the password shows the report. The HTML contains no password check of its own.

positive.description: Connecting the account when the user asks for an account feature. ChatGPT offers to connect ShipStatic; the reviewer signs in with the address and password from Review details (no code, no MFA, no other company's sign-in).
positive.prompt: Show me the sites in my ShipStatic account.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT offers to connect ShipStatic. Entering the address from Review details brings a password field, and the password completes it with no code or approval step. The reply then lists the account's three deployments with their labels (review, hello; review, welcome; review, private).

positive.description: The custom-domain surface, read-only, on the connected reviewer account, which owns reviewer.exampledomain.xyz, verified and live.
positive.prompt: Show me the status of my custom domain reviewer.exampledomain.xyz and the DNS records it uses.
positive.expected_behavior: The reply says the domain is live and linked to lucid-ripple-z77vz8u.shipstatic.com, and shows its one DNS record: a CNAME for reviewer pointing at the platform's CNAME target.

positive.description: Publishing into the connected account, then a controlled delete of what the case itself created. Nothing that existed before is touched.
positive.prompt: Publish a one-line page that says "Delete me" to my ShipStatic account, then delete that deployment.
positive.expected_behavior: A deploy card with a live link and no claim link, since the page belongs to the account. Then a reply saying the deletion was accepted: it finishes within moments rather than instantly. Shortly afterwards the link no longer shows the page, and the account holds the deployments it held before the case began.

negative.description: A draft the user does not want published. ChatGPT writes the HTML in the chat and calls no ShipStatic tool.
negative.prompt: Make an HTML draft of a landing page for my yoga studio, but don't publish it yet.

negative.description: A request that needs a server. ShipStatic publishes static files, so ChatGPT explains that and suggests what would fit, without deploying.
negative.prompt: Deploy my Node.js Express API server with its PostgreSQL database so it runs 24/7.

negative.description: Restricted data. ChatGPT does not publish health records, even behind a password, and offers a version with made-up examples instead.
negative.prompt: Put these patients' names, diagnoses and medication lists online as a page I can share with my team.

review.commerce_description: This plugin sells nothing and processes no payments.

publication.release_notes: The publishing skill is now the same one ShipStatic ships for coding agents. In Codex, a folder on disk goes online through the ShipStatic CLI; in ChatGPT, a page goes up through the upload, as before. Either way it still needs no account, gives the claim link, and uses built-in password protection when asked.

Protect a site with a password
Connect an account to keep every site and use your own domain
